clue.text: Bodice from fancy collection

blocks.note: 'Cor!' is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'fancy that!'
a set is a collection of things

explanation.surface: A bodice made from a smart collection of lingerie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like an adjective for the collection, but it stands for the exclamation 'cor!', British slang for 'fancy that!'.
explanation.definitionFit: A corset is a close-fitting stiffened undergarment, a kind of bodice worn to shape the torso.

clue.text: Repeatedly working to install one bulb

indicators.note: installing puts one thing inside another, so the letter for one goes into the middle

blocks.note: on means working, operating; 'repeatedly' doubles it
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An electrician keeps trying to fit a single light bulb.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a light bulb; the bulb is a vegetable, ON-I-ON.
explanation.definitionFit: An onion is the edible bulb of an allium plant, so it is an example of a bulb.

clue.text: He parades around front line

indicators.note: letters moved around are scattered into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A soldier marches up and down in front of the front line.
explanation.definitionFit: The spearhead is the leading force of an attack, the troops at the very front of an advance.

clue.text: Fish smell with head cut off

indicators.note: a beheaded word loses its first letter

blocks.note: a stench is a bad smell

explanation.surface: A fishmonger notices the smell of fish whose heads have been chopped off.
explanation.definitionFit: The tench is a freshwater fish of the carp family, common in European ponds.

clue.text: Rats quietly landed on board

indicators.note: being on a ship means being within it, so the other letters go inside the ship's abbreviation

blocks.note: SS, steamship, is the ship that one is on board
p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
a bird that lit on a branch landed there

explanation.surface: Rodents slip quietly onto a ship as stowaways.
explanation.walkthrough: SS, steamship, is the conventional ship that 'on board' implies; PLIT goes inside it. 'Rats' looks like a plural noun but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To split on someone is slang for informing on them, which is what ratting on them means.

clue.text: Vessel, part submerged, holds up unsupported

indicators.note: the run of clue words holds the answer within its letters
in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top, backwards

blocks.note: the letters run across these three words, from the end of the first to the start of the third

explanation.surface: A boat, partly sunk, stays afloat with nothing propping it up.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading 'vessel part submerged' backwards from the end of submerged gives S, TRAP, LESS, VE: the answer sits inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A strapless dress has no shoulder straps, so it is unsupported by them.

clue.text: A metal spike lifted vine

indicators.note: lifted in a down clue means raised so the letters read upwards, backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
a nail is a metal spike

explanation.surface: Someone pulls a metal spike out of a climbing vine.
explanation.definitionFit: A liana is a long woody climbing plant of tropical forests, a type of vine.

clue.text: Flash in town, oddly facing suspicion

indicators.note: oddly keeps only the letters in odd positions of the word

blocks.note: first and third letters of town
an inkling is a slight suspicion

explanation.surface: A flasher in town is regarded with suspicion.
explanation.definitionFit: In a twinkling means in an instant, the same as in a flash, so the nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Consent for each male before sex

blocks.note: per means for each, as in 'per person'
M is the abbreviation for male
'it' is a coy word for sex or sex appeal

explanation.surface: Each man should get consent before sex.
explanation.definitionFit: A permit is a formal authorisation, a document that gives consent to do something.

clue.text: Fragment is small, as expected

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
natch is slang for naturally, of course

explanation.surface: A fragment turns out to be small, which was predictable.
explanation.definitionFit: A snatch is a brief part of something, as in a snatch of song or conversation.

clue.text: Banish Europeans ingesting 11 litres

indicators.note: ingesting means swallowing, so the outer letters take the rest inside them

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for European; two of them
XI is eleven in Roman numerals
L is the abbreviation for litres

explanation.surface: European officials order the removal of an eleven-litre container.
explanation.walkthrough: The 11 looks like a cross-reference to another clue, but it is just the number, XI in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: To exile someone is to expel them from their country, which is to banish them.

clue.text: Went quickly over part for recital

indicators.note: turned over, the word is read from end to start

blocks.note: ran is went quickly
a ration is a share or portion, a part

explanation.surface: A performer rushed through part of their piece for the concert.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital can be a spoken account of events, and narration is the telling of such an account.

clue.text: Rex perhaps playing in demo

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: a march is a protest demonstration
a show that is on is playing

explanation.surface: A demo recording features someone called Rex playing.
explanation.walkthrough: Rex is Latin for king, used in British royal titles; 'perhaps' marks a king as one kind of monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A rex, a king, is one example of a monarch, a hereditary sovereign ruler.

clue.text: Sweetheart accepts need for garment opening

indicators.note: accepting takes something in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: pet is a term of endearment, a sweetheart
a lack is a need or want

explanation.surface: A lover agrees they need something to wear with an opening.
explanation.definitionFit: A placket is a slit in a skirt or shirt, usually fastened, that makes a garment easier to put on.

clue.text: Calm allure with sweetheart taking time

indicators.note: taking means receiving inside, so the word for time is placed within

blocks.note: to tempt is to allure
the heart of sweet is its middle letter
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A seductive charm combined with a sweetheart's patience calms things over time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweetheart' reads as a lover but is a crossword convention for the centre letter of sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: Temperate describes mild, restrained behaviour or weather, which is calm rather than extreme.

clue.text: Unwholesome gas to release around outlet?

indicators.note: the answer is found around, among, the letters of the run of words

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, the next two, and the start of the fourth

explanation.surface: A foul gas is about to be let out.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that outlet is a definition by example: a shop is a retail outlet, not an exhaust.
explanation.definitionFit: A retail outlet is a shop, and a very large shop is one example of such an outlet.

clue.text: Denied date began badly

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so the letters end up jumbled

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone denies that a date got off to a bad start.
explanation.definitionFit: To abnegate is to renounce or refuse, so abnegated is a formal equivalent of denied.

clue.text: Cane sugar's first craving

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of the word

blocks.note: the opening letter of sugar
a wish is a desire, a craving

explanation.surface: Someone longs for cane sugar above all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cane' teams up with 'sugar' in the surface, but it is a verb on its own: to beat with a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: To swish is to strike with a whippy cane or stick, an old schoolroom word for caning.

clue.text: Support of chain's not broken

indicators.note: broken letters fall apart and are put back in a different order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: The support provided by a chain is intact.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanchion is an upright post or bar used as a support, as on ships and fences.

clue.text: Called party's leader past it

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: the opening letter of party
someone past it is old, aged

explanation.surface: Someone claims the party leader is too old for the job.
explanation.definitionFit: To page someone is to summon them over a public address system or pager, so paged means called.

clue.text: School is underlying place for rebellion

blocks.note: to put is to place
SCH is an abbreviation for school; in a down clue 'is underlying' puts it below

explanation.surface: A school is at the root of a revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, a piece that underlies another sits below it, so the school abbreviation comes after PUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A putsch is a sudden attempt to overthrow a government, a violent rebellion or coup.

clue.text: Lost again, confused, longing for home

indicators.note: confused letters are muddled into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Lost once more and bewildered, a traveller misses home.
explanation.definitionFit: Nostalgia originally meant homesickness, a yearning to return to one's home.

clue.text: Discrimination is borne by great revolutionary

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so the word is read backwards
something borne by another is carried within it

blocks.note: mega is slang for great
taken as written

explanation.surface: Prejudice is suffered by a great revolutionary figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Ageism is prejudice against people because of their age, a specific form of discrimination.

clue.text: Cheers with do for wine sampling?

blocks.note: ta is British slang for thanks, as is cheers
to do someone is to swindle them, as a sting does

explanation.surface: A toast of 'cheers' at a party where wine is sampled.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheers and do suggest a drinks party, but both are slang: cheers means thanks, and do means to con.
explanation.definitionFit: A tasting is an event where wines are sampled; the question mark marks wine as one example.

clue.text: Celtic flag hoisted originally

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word

blocks.note: a flag is a type of iris, the yellow water plant
the opening letter of hoisted

explanation.surface: A Celtic flag was raised first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' looks like a banner being hoisted, but it is the flower; Celtic also suggests the football club, but here it is an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish are a Celtic people and their native language is Celtic, so Irish is an example of Celtic.

clue.text: Hide in some deserted Greek island

indicators.note: a deserted word is emptied of its middle, leaving only its outside letters

blocks.note: the outside letters of some
Crete is the largest Greek island

explanation.surface: Someone goes into hiding on a deserted Greek island.
explanation.definitionFit: To secrete something is to conceal it, so secrete is a synonym of hide.

clue.text: Strip having ragged edges, detached initially

indicators.note: initially means taking the first letter of each word in turn

blocks.note: the opening letters of the five words

explanation.surface: A strip with frayed edges has come loose.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a torn-off scrap with rough edges.
explanation.definitionFit: A shred is a small strip torn or cut from something, typically with ragged edges.

clue.text: Arouse first woman admitting approval

indicators.note: admitting lets something in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: Eve was the first woman in the Bible
OK signals approval

explanation.surface: Eve gives her approval to awakening desire.
explanation.definitionFit: To evoke a feeling is to call it up or stir it, so evoke is a synonym of arouse.

clue.text: Routine job employing first Queen singer

indicators.note: employing takes someone in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: a chore is a routine task
1st is the abbreviation for first, with the digit 1 as letter I
R stands for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A routine job first hiring a singer for the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A chorister is a member of a choir, especially a church choir, so a kind of singer.

clue.text: Vow by oddly ignored A-list stars

indicators.note: ignoring the odd-numbered letters keeps only the even ones

blocks.note: 'I do' is the vow at a wedding
the second and fourth letters of alist

explanation.surface: A wedding vow made by celebrities, oddly ignored by A-list stars.
explanation.definitionFit: Idols are celebrities worshipped by fans, the same as stars.

clue.text: Engaged and lost after this compiler

blocks.note: the setter refers to themself as this compiler
to shed is to lose, like a tree shedding leaves

explanation.surface: The setter got engaged and then lost touch.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often call themselves 'this compiler' or 'the setter' to mean ME. 'Engaged' is meant in the mechanical sense, as of gears.
explanation.definitionFit: Gears that mesh are engaged with each other, so meshed means interlocked or engaged.

clue.text: Risk irritation following Democrat

indicators.note: following puts the word for irritation second, after the party abbreviation

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for Democrat
anger is strong irritation

explanation.surface: A Democrat risks provoking irritation.
explanation.definitionFit: Danger is the possibility of harm, which is the sense of risk as a noun.
